mainTopic: Whether חופה alone creates קידושין, and the giving and wording needed for קידושין with כסף.
overview: The גמרא finishes רב הונא's argument that חופה alone can create קידושין. It first builds a קל וחומר from כסף. When that is challenged, it builds a צד השוה from כסף, ביאה and שטר. Each difference raised is knocked down by another method, and רב הונא answers the last challenge, about working against her will. רבא then brings two objections: the משנה counts only three ways, and חופה only ever completes a marriage after קידושין. אביי answers both. Next, a ברייתא teaches that קידושין with כסף works when the man gives the money and says the words. רב פפא finds a contradiction about the case where he gives and she speaks, and the גמרא gives two answers. Finally, שמואל lists which words work for קידושין and גירושין. רב פפא asks whether this means שמואל accepts unclear phrases (ידים שאין מוכיחות), and the answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Wedding canopy should surely be able to create betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends its logical argument: חופה completes a marriage, so it should be able to start one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חופה, which completes the marriage, isn't it logical that it should be able to acquire (create קידושין)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a logical argument that began just before this point. Since חופה is strong enough to finish a marriage, it should also be strong enough to create קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the end of a קל וחומר. כסף cannot complete a marriage, yet it creates קידושין. חופה can complete a marriage, so it should certainly create קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Wedding canopy; the step that completes the marriage (נִשּׂוּאִין)
Completes, finishes (the marriage)
Isn't it logical? This opens a proof by reasoning
That it should acquire, meaning it should create קידושין

phrases.english: A wedding canopy, which completes the marriage –
is it not logical that it should acquire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the קל וחומר that began before this section, which argued from כסף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: קל וחומר from כסף: if כסף, which does not complete a marriage, creates קידושין, then חופה, which does complete it, should too

steps.title: Money is special because it redeems holy items
steps.stepSummary: The proof is challenged: כסף is stronger than חופה because it can redeem הקדש and מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about money? It is special, since you can redeem consecrated property and second tithe with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof. כסף has a power that חופה does not have, so we cannot learn from כסף to חופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source is weaker than what we are learning about. כסף works in many areas, like redeeming הקדש and מעשר שני, so it may be stronger than חופה. That would break the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? The standard opening for pointing out what makes the source special
Since, because
Redeem
Property consecrated to the Temple (הקדש)
Second tithe, which can be redeemed with money

phrases.english: What about money? It is special, since one redeems with it
consecrated property and second tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְכֶסֶף, שֶׁכֵּן פּוֹדִין בּוֹ הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from כסף to חופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כסף has a broad power (redeeming הקדש and מעשר שני) that חופה lacks, so כסף may be stronger and we cannot learn from it.

steps.title: Intercourse shows that this power is not needed
steps.stepSummary: ביאה cannot redeem anything, yet it creates קידושין, so redeeming power is not the key.
steps.simpleTranslation: Intercourse proves otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to ביאה. ביאה does not redeem holy items, yet it still creates קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said only something as strong as כסף can create קידושין. ביאה shows that is wrong, because it has no redeeming power and still works. So חופה should not be blocked for lacking that power either.

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations, one of the three ways to create קידושין
Will prove (otherwise); used to bring a counter-example

phrases.english: Intercourse will prove otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 with a counter-example.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a method as strong as כסף, which redeems holy items, can create קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: ביאה creates קידושין without any redeeming power, so that power is not what matters.

steps.title: Intercourse is special because it acquires a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: ביאה is challenged: it has its own special power, since it acquires a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about intercourse? It is special, since it acquires a יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the proof from ביאה. ביאה also has a special strength that חופה does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבם acquires his יבמה through ביאה, not through חופה. So ביאה may be stronger than חופה, and we cannot learn חופה from ביאה either.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died childless, who becomes linked to his brother (the יָבָם)
Acquires

phrases.english: What about intercourse? It is special, since it acquires a yevama.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the counter-example from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ביאה as a source for חופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביאה has a unique power (acquiring a יבמה) that חופה lacks, so ביאה may be stronger.

steps.title: Money shows that the יבמה power is not needed
steps.stepSummary: כסף cannot acquire a יבמה, yet it creates קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money proves otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to כסף as the answer. כסף cannot acquire a יבמה, yet it still creates קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source has a strength the other lacks. כסף's strength was answered by ביאה, and ביאה's strength is answered by כסף. This sets up the next move, a proof from what they share.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (otherwise)

phrases.english: Money will prove otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 with a counter-example.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a method that can acquire a יבמה creates קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: כסף creates קידושין without acquiring a יבמה, so that power is not needed.

steps.title: Proof from what money and intercourse share
steps.stepSummary: Since כסף and ביאה each have their own special feature, the גמרא learns from what they share: they acquire elsewhere and create קידושין, so חופה should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back around. This one is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that they acquire in other settings and also acquire here. So I will bring חופה, which acquires in other settings, and say it acquires here too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a new kind of proof, a צד השוה. It ignores what makes כסף and ביאה special and looks only at what they share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source's special strength was cancelled out by the other source. What is left is the shared feature: both work elsewhere and both create קידושין. חופה also works elsewhere, so it should also create קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument has returned (to the starting point)
The feature of this one is not like the feature of that one
The common feature; a proof from what two sources share
In general, in other settings
I too will bring (the new case)

steps.whatToRemember: A צד השוה proof: when two sources each have a weakness, but the weakness of each is cancelled by the other, we learn from their shared feature.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a קל וחומר anymore. It does not say חופה is stronger. It only says חופה shares the same feature as כסף and ביאה.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around:
the aspect of this one is not like the aspect of that one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is כסף and "that one" is ביאה; each has its own special feature.

phrases.english: and the aspect of that one is not like the aspect of this one;
the common feature between them is:
that they acquire elsewhere and they acquire here,
so I too will bring a wedding canopy
which acquires elsewhere, and so it acquires here.
phrases.notes: For חופה, "elsewhere" means after קידושין, where it makes her fully married.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth of steps 2-5, builds a new proof from the shared feature of כסף and ביאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: צד השוה of כסף and ביאה: both acquire elsewhere and create קידושין

steps.title: Money and intercourse both give great benefit
steps.stepSummary: The צד השוה is challenged: כסף and ביאה share another feature, great benefit, which חופה lacks.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the common feature between them? They share that their benefit is great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the צד השוה proof. Maybe what really makes כסף and ביאה work is that the woman gets a lot of benefit from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צד השוה fails if the two sources share another feature that the new case lacks. Both כסף and ביאה give great benefit or pleasure. חופה may not, so it might not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Their benefit or pleasure
Great, large

phrases.english: What about the common feature between them?
They are special, since their benefit is great.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְצַד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן הֲנָאָתָן מְרוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the צד השוה proof of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The צד השוה of כסף and ביאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share great benefit, which חופה may lack, so that may be the real reason they work.

steps.title: A document shows great benefit is not needed
steps.stepSummary: שטר gives no great benefit, yet it creates קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A document proves otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with שטר, the third way to create קידושין. A document gives the woman little benefit, yet it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If great benefit were needed, שטר would not work. Since שטר does work, benefit is not the key, and חופה can still be learned.

keyTerms.meaning: A document; one of the three ways to create קידושין

phrases.english: A document will prove otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 with a counter-example.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a method that gives great benefit can create קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: שטר creates קידושין with no great benefit, so benefit is not needed.

steps.title: A document is special because it can end a marriage
steps.stepSummary: שטר is challenged: it has a special power, since a גט ends a marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a document? It is special, since it releases a Jewish woman from marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from שטר. A document can also be a גט, so it has a strength that חופה does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a document can end a marriage, maybe that is why it can also start one. חופה cannot end a marriage, so we cannot learn it from שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: Releases, takes out (of marriage), as a גֵּט does
A Jewish woman

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִשְׁטָר, שֶׁכֵּן מוֹצִיא בְּבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: What about a document? It is special, since it releases a Jewish woman from marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִשְׁטָר, שֶׁכֵּן מוֹצִיא בְּבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the counter-example from step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שטר has a unique power (ending a marriage as a גט) that חופה lacks, so שטר may be stronger.

steps.title: Money and intercourse show ending a marriage is not needed
steps.stepSummary: כסף and ביאה cannot end a marriage, yet they create קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money and intercourse prove otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with כסף and ביאה together. Neither can end a marriage, yet both create קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The power to end a marriage is not needed to create קידושין, since כסף and ביאה work without it. Now every special feature has been cancelled out, setting up the final restatement.

keyTerms.meaning: They will prove (otherwise); plural form

phrases.english: Money and intercourse will prove otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 with a counter-example.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a method that can end a marriage creates קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: כסף and ביאה create קידושין without being able to end a marriage, so that power is not needed.

steps.title: The common-feature proof restated for wedding canopy
steps.stepSummary: With all the special features cancelled out, the גמרא restates the צד השוה: these methods acquire elsewhere and create קידושין, so חופה should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back around. This one is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that they acquire elsewhere and acquire here. So I will bring חופה, which acquires elsewhere, and say it acquires here too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the צד השוה proof, now that the new challenge (great benefit) has been answered. The conclusion again is that חופה should create קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "great benefit" challenge was answered by שטר, and the שטר challenge was answered by כסף and ביאה. So only the shared feature remains: acquiring elsewhere and creating קידושין. חופה has that feature, so the proof stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: They acquire (plural)
Here, meaning for קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: After two rounds of challenges and counter-examples, the צד השוה proof still stands: חופה, like כסף, ביאה and שטר, works elsewhere and so should create קידושין.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around:
the aspect of this one is not like the aspect of that one,
and the aspect of that one is not like the aspect of this one;
the common feature between them is:
that they acquire elsewhere and they acquire here –
so I too will bring a wedding canopy,
which acquires elsewhere, and so it acquires here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the צד השוה proof of step 6, now that the challenges of steps 7 and 9 have been answered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: צד השוה of the methods that create קידושין: they acquire elsewhere and also acquire here

steps.title: All three methods can work against her will
steps.stepSummary: The צד השוה is challenged again: כסף, שטר and ביאה can each work against a woman's will in some case, but חופה cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the feature all three share: each of them can work against her will?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds one more feature that כסף, שטר and ביאה share and חופה lacks. So the צד השוה may not carry over to חופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each method works against a woman's will somewhere: a גט (a שטר) is given without her agreement, ביאה acquires a יבמה without her agreement, and a father can sell his daughter as an אמה עבריה with כסף. חופה only works when she enters willingly. So maybe this power is why the three create קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: against her will
the common feature shared by several sources
a widow who must marry her late husband's brother
a Jewish maidservant sold by her father

phrases.english: What about the common feature among them,
that they work against her will?
phrases.notes: A גט is given without her agreement, a יבמה is taken with ביאה, and a father sells his daughter for כסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the restated צד השוה from step 11 with a new shared feature.
steps.kashyaTarget: The צד השוה derivation of חופה from כסף, שטר and ביאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three sources share a power (working against her will) that חופה lacks, so the derivation can be broken.

steps.title: In marriage, money never works against her will
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that כסף, when used for marriage, never works against the woman's will.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא would say: we have not found that money works against her will when it is used for marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his צד השוה. He points out that כסף only works against her will for an אמה עבריה, not for marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge used the case of an אמה עבריה, but that is not marriage. In marriage itself, כסף needs the woman's agreement, just like חופה. So 'against her will' is not a feature all three sources share in marriage, and the צד השוה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: marriage
at least, in any case
we have not found

phrases.english: And רב הונא would answer:
money at least, in marriage,
we have not found working against her will.

steps.whatToRemember: With every special feature cancelled out, רב הונא's צד השוה survives: חופה should create קידושין like כסף, שטר and ביאה.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא כֶּסֶף מִיהָא בְּאִישׁוּת לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן בְּעַל כׇּרְחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope: the case raised (אמה עבריה) is not marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three sources can work against her will, so חופה cannot be derived from them.
steps.terutzMaskana: In marriage, כסף needs her agreement, so the shared feature fails and the derivation holds.

steps.title: The משנה counts three ways, not four
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives two objections to רב הונא. The first is that the משנה says a woman is acquired in three ways, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: there are two objections to this. One is that we learned 'three' in the משנה, and we did not learn 'four.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins attacking רב הונא's whole idea and announces that he has two objections. His first objection is that the משנה lists only three ways to acquire a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a woman is acquired in three ways: כסף, שטר and ביאה. If חופה also created קידושין, there would be four. Since the משנה gives a number, it seems to mean no other way exists.

keyTerms.meaning: two objections or refutations
one (the first point)

phrases.english: רבא said:
There are two objections to this matter.
One: that we learned 'three,'
phrases.notes: This points to the opening words of our משנה: a woman is acquired in three ways.

phrases.english: and we did not learn 'four.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the צד השוה survives, רבא attacks רב הונא's position from a new angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that חופה creates קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's number 'three' leaves out חופה, which means a fourth way does not exist.

steps.title: חופה only finishes a marriage that קידושין started
steps.stepSummary: רבא's second objection: every חופה we know of comes after קידושין, so we cannot learn from it that חופה works without קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: doesn't חופה only complete a marriage after קידושין? Can we learn a חופה without קידושין from a חופה that comes after קידושין?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the starting point of רב הונא's proof. רב הונא had argued that חופה is strong, because it finishes a marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's קל וחומר said that if חופה finishes a marriage, it should surely be able to start one. רבא answers that חופה finishes a marriage only because קידושין already happened. Without קידושין, we have no proof that חופה has any power at all.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore (a second point)
completes, finishes (the marriage)
isn't it so that (opening a challenging question)
we learn or derive

phrases.english: And furthermore: does חופה complete the marriage
other than through קידושין?
And can we learn a חופה
that comes without קידושין
from a חופה that comes after קידושין?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד כְּלוּם חוּפָּה גּוֹמֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is רבא's second objection, announced in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basis of רב הונא's קל וחומר: that חופה finishes a marriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חופה's power to finish a marriage depends on קידושין that came before it, so it cannot show that חופה works alone.

steps.title: The משנה lists only what the תורה writes clearly
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבא's first objection: the משנה lists only ways written clearly in the תורה, and חופה is not one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: about what you said, that we learned 'three' and not 'four': the תנא teaches something written clearly, and does not teach something not written clearly.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבא's first objection about the number 'three' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list is not meant to cover every way. It includes only the methods the תורה writes clearly. חופה is learned through reasoning (the קל וחומר), so leaving it out of the count proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: the teacher of the משנה
clearly, openly
a matter, a thing

phrases.english: אביי said to him: That which you said,
'we learned three and did not learn four':
the תנא teaches a matter that is written clearly,
phrases.notes: He means written clearly in the תורה.

phrases.english: a matter that is not written clearly
he does not teach.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי has answered only רבא's first objection here. He answers the second objection, about חופה needing קידושין, in the next step.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי הָא דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ שָׁלֹשׁ תְּנַן וְאַרְבַּע לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's first objection from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the משנה's list: it covers only methods written clearly in the תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number 'three' means there are only three ways, so חופה cannot be a fourth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list covers only clearly written methods. חופה comes from reasoning, so the count does not rule it out.

steps.title: Answering the second objection: the proof uses the fact that חופה comes after קידושין
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבא's second objection. רב הונא never claimed we have seen חופה work without קידושין. His קל וחומר is actually built on the fact that חופה finishes a marriage after כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said that חופה only finishes a marriage after קידושין. That is exactly רב הונא's point. כסף cannot finish a marriage after כסף, yet it still acquires a woman. So חופה, which can finish a marriage after כסף, should surely be able to acquire her too.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues and answers רבא's second objection. He shows it is really part of רב הונא's argument. It is not a hole in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that every חופה we know of comes after קידושין. אביי replies that this fact is the very thing that makes חופה strong. A second gift of כסף cannot bring a woman into נישואין, but חופה can. If the weaker כסף can still make קידושין, the stronger חופה should be able to as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Completes, meaning it brings the woman into full marriage (נישואין)
The full marriage stage that comes after קידושין
A reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one: if the weaker can do it, the stronger surely can
Is it not logical? This is the phrase that closes a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: חופה's power to finish a marriage after קידושין is the source of its strength in רב הונא's קל וחומר. It is not a weakness.

phrases.english: And as for what you said: "Does a wedding canopy complete a marriage
except by means of betrothal?"
Rav Huna is also saying exactly this:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה כֶּסֶף שֶׁאֵינוֹ גּוֹמֵר אַחַר כֶּסֶף – קוֹנֶה,
phrases.english: If money, which does not complete a marriage after money, acquires,
phrases.notes: Giving her a second gift of money after the קידושין money does not make her fully married.

phrases.english: then a wedding canopy, which does complete a marriage after money,
is it not logical that it should acquire?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ כְּלוּם חוּפָּה גּוֹמֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 16 answered רבא's first objection. This step answers his second.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the objection's premise is part of the proof itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חופה is only ever seen after קידושין, we cannot learn that it works by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: חופה's ability to finish a marriage after כסף makes it stronger than כסף, so a קל וחומר teaches that it can acquire by itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא on how קידושין through כסף works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that קידושין through כסף works when the man gives money and says one of several formulas. If the woman gives the money and she says the words, there is no קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is קידושין done with money? If he gave her money or something worth money and said, "You are מקודשת to me," or "You are מאורסת to me," or "You are mine as a wife," she is מקודשת. But if she gave and she said, "I am מקודשת to you," "I am מאורסת to you," or "I am yours as a wife," she is not מקודשת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that explains the details of קידושין with כסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things are needed: the man gives the money, and the man says the words. Any of the three phrases works. When the roles are reversed and the woman both gives and speaks, it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Something worth money, such as an object
Betrothed. This is another word for מקודשת
Aramaic for "as a wife"

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that in קידושין the man is the one who acquires. That is why his giving matters.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: How is betrothal done through money?

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לָהּ כֶּסֶף אוֹ שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף,
phrases.english: If he gave her money or something worth money,
and said to her: "You are hereby betrothed to me,"
or "You are hereby engaged to me,"

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵי אַתְּ לִי לְאִינְתּוּ״ – הֲרֵי זוֹ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: or "You are mine as a wife": she is betrothed.
But if she is the one who gave, and she said:
"I am hereby betrothed to you," "I am hereby engaged to you,"
or "I am yours as a wife": she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the sources for the ways of acquiring, the גמרא turns to the practical details of קידושין through כסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he gives and he says the words, she is מקודשת. If she gives and she says the words, she is not.

steps.title: רב פפא finds a contradiction between the two halves of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא looks at the middle case, where he gives and she speaks. The first half of the ברייתא suggests she is not מקודשת, but the second half suggests she is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: The first half works only because he gave and he spoke. That implies that if he gave and she spoke, she is not מקודשת. Now look at the second half: it fails only because she gave and she spoke. That implies that if he gave and she spoke, it is קידושין!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא reads both halves of the ברייתא closely and shows that they point to opposite answers for the same in-between case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither half talks directly about the case where he gives and she speaks. The first half says the case works because he did both things, so if she speaks, it should fail. The second half says the case fails because she did both things, so if only she speaks, it should work. Both readings cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it. This phrase introduces a strong objection
The reason. Here it means: "the only reason it works is..."
This implies. It draws a conclusion from what the text did not say
The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The case being argued about (he gives, she speaks) is never stated in the ברייתא. רב פפא is only working out what each half implies about it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to this:
The reason is that he gave and he said,

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָתַן הוּא וְאָמְרָה הִיא – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: which implies that if he gave and she said, she is not betrothed.
Now say the last part:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הִיא שֶׁנָּתְנָה לוֹ וְאָמְרָה הִיא –
phrases.english: "But if she gave to him and she said,
it is not a betrothal."
The reason is that she gave and she said,

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָתַן הוּא וְאָמְרָה הִיא – הָווּ קִידּוּשִׁין!
phrases.english: which implies that if he gave and she said, it is a betrothal!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא טַעְמָא דְּנָתַן הוּא וְאָמַר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inferences from the רישא and the סיפא lead to opposite rulings for the case where he gives and she speaks.

steps.title: Only the first half is exact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the רישא is worded exactly, while the סיפא was just phrased to mirror the first half. So we should not draw inferences from the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part is exact. The last part was just stated that way for no special reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to solve רב פפא's contradiction by saying we should only trust the inference from the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the סיפא's wording is not exact, its hidden implication disappears. That leaves the רישא's implication standing: if he gives and she speaks, she is not מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: Exact. We can draw conclusions from its precise wording
Stated for no special reason; the wording just copies the pattern of the first half

phrases.english: The first part is exact,
the last part was taken for no reason.
phrases.notes: The second half was just worded to match the first, so don't read anything into its exact words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers רב פפא's contradiction from Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting which part of the text is precise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves of the ברייתא are exact, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the רישא is exact. If he gives and she speaks, she is not מקודשת.

steps.title: Would the ברייתא really contradict itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. It is hard to accept that a ברייתא would word its second half in a way that implies the opposite of its first half.
steps.simpleTranslation: But would the ברייתא really teach, in its last part, something that contradicts its first part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. This sets up the next move, where a better solution will be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a phrase is "not exact" is one thing. Saying it was worded so that it actually suggests the opposite ruling is much harder to accept. So the answer from Step 20 is now in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Contradicts
A matter or a statement

phrases.aramaic: וְתָנֵי סֵיפָא מִילְּתָא דְּסָתְרָא לַהּ לְרֵישָׁא?
phrases.english: And would the last part teach something that contradicts the first part?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנֵי סֵיפָא מִילְּתָא דְּסָתְרָא לַהּ לְרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the answer given in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the סיפא is worded loosely (כדי נסבה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Loose wording might be acceptable, but wording that implies the opposite ruling of the רישא is unreasonable for a ברייתא.

steps.title: New reading: he gives and she speaks counts as if she did both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the idea that the סיפא is just echo wording. It explains that the ברייתא treats 'he gave, she said' exactly like 'she gave, she said,' so there is no קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the ברייתא means: if he gave and he said, it is obviously קידושין. If he gave and she said, it is treated as if she gave and she said, so it is not קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fresh answer to רב פפא's question about the middle case. The סיפא, 'she gave and she said,' really includes the case where he gave and she said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 rejected the idea that the סיפא was worded only to match the רישא. Now the סיפא is read as a real teaching: once she is the one who says the words, the קידושין fails, even if he handed over the money. That settles the clash: the middle case is no קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means: drops an earlier reading and gives a new one
Obvious
It is treated as if

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
If he gave and he said,
it is obvious that it is a valid betrothal.
If he gave and she said,

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁנָּתְנָה הִיא וְאָמְרָה הִיא,
phrases.english: it is treated as if she gave and she said,
and it is not a valid betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 21 with a new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא so that one clause includes the middle case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא was only worded to mirror the רישא, so nothing can be learned from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is exact: if she speaks, even when he gave, it is treated as if she did everything, and there is no קידושין.

steps.title: Second reading: the middle case is a doubt
steps.stepSummary: Another way to read the ברייתא: he gave and he said is קידושין, she gave and she said is not, and he gave and she said is a ספק, so we worry about it מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: if he gave and he said, she is מקודשת. If she gave and she said, she is not מקודשת. If he gave and she said, it is a doubt, and we worry about it by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different answer to the same question. It says the ברייתא gives no firm ruling on the middle case, because that case is unsure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That is why the רישא seems to suggest no קידושין and the סיפא seems to suggest קידושין: each clause only fully covers its own clear case. Since the middle case is a ספק, חז"ל tell us to treat it as a possible קידושין to be careful.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces a second answer
A doubt; the law is unsure
We worry about it and act carefully
By rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. In the first answer, 'he gave, she said' is NOT קידושין. In the second answer, it is a ספק and we act strictly מדרבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: The middle case, where he gives and she speaks, has two readings: no קידושין at all, or a ספק that we worry about מדרבנן.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
If he gave and he said, she is betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: נָתְנָה הִיא וְאָמְרָה הִיא – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: If she gave and she said, she is not betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן הוּא וְאָמְרָה הִיא – סְפֵיקָא הִיא
phrases.english: If he gave and she said, it is a doubt,
and we worry about it by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question that Step 22 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Treating the middle case as an unresolved doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the ברייתא give opposite rulings for the middle case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither half rules on the middle case. It is a ספק, and we act strictly מדרבנן.

steps.title: שמואל: which words work for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that phrases describing her as betrothed work for קידושין. Phrases describing him as her husband do not work at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: in קידושין, if he gave her money or something worth money and said 'You are מקודשת,' 'You are מאורסת,' or 'You are a wife,' she is מקודשת. If he said 'I am your man,' 'I am your husband,' or 'I am your betrothed,' there is nothing to worry about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from שמואל about the wording of קידושין. The words must describe her as becoming his, not him as becoming hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The good phrases all put the change on her: she becomes betrothed, a wife. The bad phrases put it on him, and the תורה describes the man taking the woman, not the reverse. Those bad phrases are so useless that we don't even treat them as a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: Something worth money
Betrothed (another word for מקודשת)
As a wife
There is nothing to worry about here, not even a doubt

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that the words of קידושין must describe the woman being acquired, not the man.

phrases.english: Shmuel says: With regard to betrothal,
if he gave her money or something worth money
and said to her: 'You are hereby betrothed,'
'You are hereby betrothed (me'oreset),'
'You are hereby as a wife,'
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'to me' in the round brackets and some leave it out. Without it, the question in Step 26 makes more sense.

phrases.english: she is betrothed.
'I am hereby your man,' 'I am hereby your husband,' 'I am hereby your betrothed,'
there is no room for concern here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from who gives and who speaks to which exact words work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Phrases that make her betrothed work. Phrases that make him her husband do not work at all.

steps.title: שמואל: which words work for גירושין
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives the same rule for divorce. Phrases that release her work, and phrases about him not being her husband do nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same in divorce: if he gave her a גט and said 'You are sent away,' 'You are divorced,' or 'You are permitted to any man,' she is divorced. If he said 'I am not your man,' 'I am not your husband,' or 'I am not your betrothed,' there is nothing to worry about.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל continues his teaching and applies the same rule to גירושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like in קידושין, the divorce words must speak about her: she is released and free to marry. Saying that he is no longer her husband puts the change on him, so it means nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Divorce
Sent away
Permitted to marry any man

steps.whatToRemember: For both קידושין and גירושין, שמואל requires the words to describe the woman's status, not the man's.

phrases.english: And similarly, with regard to divorce,
if he gave her and said to her:
phrases.notes: He gave her the גט; the גמרא doesn't spell it out.

phrases.english: 'You are hereby sent away,' 'You are hereby divorced,'
'You are hereby permitted to any man,'
she is divorced.
'I am not your man,' 'I am not your husband,' 'I am not your betrothed,'
there is no room for concern here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's statement and applies the same rule to divorce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce words must release her. Words saying he is not her husband do nothing.

steps.title: Does שמואל accept unclear, incomplete phrases?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי whether שמואל's ruling shows that he holds ידים שאין מוכיחות work, since 'You are מקודשת' never says 'to me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Does this mean שמואל holds that unclear partial phrases count as real phrases?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges שמואל's ruling. The man said 'You are מקודשת' without adding 'to me,' so the words don't say who she is betrothed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יד is a partial phrase that stands for the full act. If it doesn't make the meaning clear on its own, it is a יד שאינה מוכחת, and whether that works is a known dispute. רב פפא is pointing out that שמואל seems to take a side on that dispute, which sets up an answer next.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? Draws a surprising conclusion from a ruling
Partial phrases that stand for a full act (literally 'hands' or handles)
Unclear partial phrases that don't show the full meaning by themselves

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Is this to say that Shmuel holds
that unclear partial phrases count as partial phrases?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: לְמֵימְרָא דְּסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what שמואל's list of valid phrases says about his view on unclear phrases.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that 'You are מקודשת' works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase leaves out 'to me,' so it is unclear. Validating it seems to mean שמואל holds ידים שאין מוכיחות work, a disputed position he may not hold.

steps.title: The נזיר case shows שמואל needs a clear context
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings שמואל's own ruling in נזיר. There, 'I will be' works only when a נזיר is passing by. So שמואל seems to hold that unclear phrases do not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: someone who says 'I will be' is a נזיר. We asked about this: maybe he meant 'I will be fasting'? And שמואל said: the משנה is talking about a case where a נזיר was passing in front of him. So the only reason it works is that a נזיר was passing by. Without that, it would not work!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his question from step 26. He shows that in another place, שמואל did not accept an unclear phrase unless the situation made it clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I will be' is an incomplete phrase, just like 'You are מקודשת' without 'to me.' שמואל said it works only when a passing נזיר makes the meaning obvious. That means unclear phrases do not work alone, which clashes with his קידושין ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who takes a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
And we discussed it, meaning we raised a question about it
A fast
Passing in front of him
But if not for this, it would not work. The גמרא is drawing a 'without this, no' inference

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's statement in נזיר does not say outright that unclear phrases fail. רב פפא is drawing that from the fact that שמואל needed the passing נזיר to make the vow work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real contradiction inside שמואל's own rulings. The גמרא has to explain why 'You are מקודשת' works without 'to me.'

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: one who says 'I will be'
phrases.notes: This is the משנה at the start of נזיר (2a).

phrases.english: he is a נזיר.
And we discussed it:
But maybe he is saying 'I will be fasting'?
And שמואל said,
this is when a נזיר was passing in front of him.
The reason is that a נזיר is passing in front of him,
but if not so, it would not work!
phrases.notes: In other words, without the passing נזיר, plain 'I will be' would mean nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פפא's question by bringing proof that שמואל holds unclear phrases do not work.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that 'You are מקודשת' works for קידושין (step 24)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In נזיר, שמואל needed a clear setting to make an incomplete phrase work. So he holds unclear phrases fail, which should also make 'You are מקודשת' without 'to me' fail.

steps.title: שמואל's case is where he said 'to me'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל's קידושין ruling is about a man who added 'to me.' So no unclear phrase is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he said 'to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא. It explains that שמואל's קידושין case includes the words 'to me.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he says 'You are מקודשת to me,' the phrase is complete and clear. So שמואל's קידושין ruling says nothing about unclear phrases, and it no longer clashes with his ruling in נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A way of narrowing a statement to a specific case
To me

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where he said 'to me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge by narrowing שמואל's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling was about a man who said only 'You are מקודשת,' with no 'to me.'
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's ruling is about a man who said 'to me,' so it does not depend on unclear phrases working.

steps.title: Then what is שמואל teaching us?
steps.stepSummary: If the man said 'to me,' the קידושין obviously works. So what new point is שמואל teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. If he said the full phrase, שמואל's ruling seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A complete phrase like 'You are מקודשת to me' clearly works. If that were all שמואל meant, his statement would teach nothing new, so the גמרא asks what his point is.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What is he teaching us? Asked when a statement seems obvious

phrases.english: If so,
what is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 28 by saying it makes שמואל's ruling pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמואל's case is one where he said 'to me' (step 28)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full phrase with 'to me' obviously works, so שמואל would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The answer begins with 'these'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to explain what שמואל is teaching. Only the first word, 'these,' appears here, and the rest comes next.
